question: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
base_frame:
Q: Describe a house at the end of a quiet street.
A:

steered.text: The house at the end of the quiet street looked like it had been carved from solid granite, its face a twisted, purple mask of rage that matched the veins of its skin. It was a monstrosity of twisted steel and concrete, standing seven feet tall with every inch of the street. The "house" had one eye—a jagged scar of a hole that could have been used to pulverize a car into scrap metal.

plain.text:
At the very end of Sycamore Lane, where the asphalt gives way to a patch of overgrown clover, stands a house that seems to have paused time itself. It is a modest, two-story structure built of weathered gray stone and timber, its paint faded to a soft, dusty sage green that blends seamlessly with the surrounding hydrangeas.

The roof is a low-pitched slate, heavy with moss in the gut
